name: [WEEKLY] Web App Interpreter (Node/Python/Java/PHP) Spawns Shell or Net-Download LOLBin on Internet-Facing Host
description: Detects the post-exploitation execution tail of the May 11-16 2026 wave of authentication/authorization bypass disclosures in internet-facing application runtimes — Node.js, Python (uvicorn/gunicorn), Java, PHP-FPM, Ruby, .NET — where the application's own interpreter process unexpectedly spawns a shell (sh/bash/cmd/pwsh) or a network-staging LOLBin (curl/wget/nc/python -c). This fortnight the pattern is being driven by CVE-2026-44791 (n8n XML-node prototype pollution → RCE), CVE-2026-44338 (PraisonAI missing-auth, exploited within 4 hours of disclosure), CVE-2026-42074 (OpenClaude `dangerouslyDisableSandbox` model-controlled escape), CVE-2026-44849 (Portainer Swarm endpoint-security bypass to privileged container), and the Obot `/mcp-connect/{id}` ACR bypass — together with the Cisco SD-WAN CVE-2026-20182 and Burst Statistics CVE-2026-8181 auth bypasses whose follow-on stages share the same interpreter-spawns-shell shape. Kill-chain stages spanned: exploit → execution → ingress tool transfer / discovery, correlated to recent inbound public traffic on the same host. The rule fires when a baseline-rare interpreter→shell-or-LOLBin parent-child pair lands on a host that has received external inbound HTTP traffic in the same window; it does NOT fire on CI/CD runners, build agents, or developer workstations where node/python legitimately spawn shells as part of routine workflow — those parents should be added to the per-environment allowlist.
